extracted.intended_audience: Users of GAP and computational/group-theory researchers working with character tables and permutation characters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for representing Molien series, identifying and testing possible permutation characters, computing power maps, and related computations on character tables using GAP. Targets GAP users performing character-table based subgroup/subaction inference and modular representation checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Molien series denominator representation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the rational function ratfun was constructed by MolienSeries, a representation as quotient of polynomials is known such that the denominator is a product of terms of the form (1 - z^r)^k. This information is encoded as value of MolienSeriesInfo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MolienSeriesInfo returns a record describing the rational function with components numer, denom, ratfun, numerstring, denomstring, denominfo (a list [[r1,k1],..., [rn,kn]] such that denom = ∏ (1 - z^{ri})^{ki}), summands (records with numer, r, k for summands numer/(1-z^r)^k), pol (final polynomial), size (order of underlying matrix group), degree (degree of underlying representation). A special PrintObj method exists for Molien series. MolienSeriesWithGivenDenominator can try to view a Molien series using a prescribed list of r's; it fails if not representable that way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible permutation character — being a G-character
rubrics_metrics.description: π is a character of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the basic requirement: the class function must be a genuine character (integer combination of irreducibles as appropriate). (Condition (a) in the listing from Isaacs.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible permutation character — nonnegative integer values
rubrics_metrics.description: π(g) is a nonnegative integer for all g ∈ G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All values of π on group elements must be nonnegative integers (condition (b)). TestPerm1 checks related constraints (returns codes if violated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible permutation character — degree divides group order
rubrics_metrics.description: π(1) divides |G|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The degree (value at identity) must be a divisor of the group order (condition (c)). TestPerm2 includes checks related to degree divisibility in some formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible permutation character — monotonic on powers
rubrics_metrics.description: π(g^n) ≥ π(g) for g ∈ G and integers n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values on powers of an element cannot decrease: π evaluated at powers is at least the value at the element (condition (d)). Note: (d) is checked only for those power maps that are stored in the character table of G; if it holds for stored prime-power maps it then holds for all integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible permutation character — transitivity scalar product
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scalar product with the trivial character equals 1, i.e., π contains the trivial constituent exactly once — corresponding to permutation characters of transitive actions (condition (e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible permutation character — multiplicity bound for rational irreducibles
rubrics_metrics.description: The multiplicity of any rational irreducible G-character ψ as a constituent of π is at most ψ(1)/[ψ,ψ].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This bounds multiplicities of rational irreducible constituents (condition (f)). GAP checks this when computing possible permutation characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible permutation character — vanishing for incompatible orders
rubrics_metrics.description: π(g) = 0 if the order of g does not divide |G|/π(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the element order does not divide the index of the assumed stabilizer (|G|/π(1)), then π must vanish on that class (condition (g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible permutation character — class value divisibility condition
rubrics_metrics.description: π(1)|N_G(g)| divides π(g)|G| for all g ∈ G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A divisibility relation between centralizer sizes, π-values and group order must hold for every class (condition (h)). This is used to restrict possibilities for images and class lengths in putative subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible permutation character — upper bound on class values
rubrics_metrics.description: π(g) ≤ (|G| − π(1)) / (|g^G| |Gal_G(g)|) for all nonidentity g ∈ G, where |Gal_G(g)| is the number of conjugacy classes of G that contain generators of ⟨g⟩.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an explicit numerical upper bound for π(g) in terms of conjugacy class lengths and Galois-related class counts (condition (i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible permutation character — Sylow p constraints (single p-power factor)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p is a prime that divides |G|/π(1) only once then s/(p − 1) divides |G|/π(1) and is congruent to 1 modulo p, where s is the number of elements of order p in the hypothetical subgroup H for which π = (1_H)^G holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constraint (condition (j)) relates the number of elements of order p in the subgroup to arithmetic congruences; it can rule out impossible degrees or distributions of p-elements. Note s/(p-1) equals number of Sylow p-subgroups in H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of 'possible permutation character' in GAP
rubrics_metrics.description: Any G-class function with the properties (a)–(j) is called a possible permutation character in GAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAP provides algorithms (PermChars) to compute such class functions; passing these initial tests does not guarantee existence of a subgroup realizing the character, but failure implies nonexistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: PermCharInfo output components (contained, bound, display, ATLAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a permutation character ψ = (1_U)^G or list thereof, PermCharInfo returns components: contained (numbers of elements of U in each class), bound (divisors of class lengths in U), display (record usable by Display to show perm chars and the contained/bound where nonzero), ATLAS (Atlas-like decomposition strings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: contained[i] = ψ[i]|U| / SizesCentralizers(tbl)[i]. bound[i] = |U|/gcd(|U|, SizesCentralizers(tbl)[i]). ATLAS encodes decomposition into irreducibles using degree labels and letter indices; formatting choices include 'LaTeX' or 'HTML' options for exponent notation. PermCharInfo helps infer subgroup information (class membership counts, decomposition). Example outputs are shown for A6 and J1 in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: PermChars behavior and algorithm selection guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: PermChars(tbl[, cond]) returns the list of all possible permutation characters of tbl matching properties described by optional cond. The algorithm depends on cond and may be computationally heavy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called with only tbl returns all possible permutation characters (may be long and slow); user is encouraged to try different cond options. If cond is a positive integer, PermChars returns characters of that degree, using a preprocessing step (PermBounds) requiring inversion of the rational character table (restricted to tables with <~100 classes). If cond is a record, components like degree, torso, chars, normalsubgroup, nonfaithful can restrict the search and change the algorithm. An empty list denotes no possible permutation character with those properties. Use of ineq (Inequalities) and other preprocessing can speed search. Examples include computing PermChars(m11) returning 39 possibilities and PermChars(m11,220) returning specific characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: PermChars torso and normalsubgroup / nonfaithful constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: If cond.torso is provided (a list with known values at positions) and optionally normalsubgroup (class positions of normal subgroup N) and nonfaithful (a possible permutation character π), PermChars returns characters agreeing with torso on bound positions and with the property that no irreducible constituent of ψ−π has N in its kernel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This forces computed characters ψ to be compatible with a known kernel containment N ≤ V where π=(1_V)^G and enforces that if ψ=(1_U)^G then V = U N. Use when some values or kernel structure is known to prune search.

rubrics_metrics.name: PermChars 'chars' option semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: If cond.chars is bound, it should contain all rational irreducible characters that might be constituents of the required characters; if it omits some characters, GAP checks scalar products with omitted irreducibles are nonnegative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only omit characters if there are good reasons; otherwise include full Irr(tbl). When chars is bound, PermChars may perform extra checks to ensure compatibility with omitted constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestPerm1 checks (T1/T2) and return codes
rubrics_metrics.description: TestPerm1(tbl, char) implements tests corresponding to conditions (b) and (d): nonnegativity and monotonicity on powers. It returns 1 or 2 if char fails because of (T1) or (T2) respectively, and 0 if the character satisfies the conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those power maps stored on tbl are considered for (T2). Use TestPerm1 to filter obvious non-candidates early. Example: applied to rationalized combinations of irreducibles in A5 produced specific return codes in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestPerm2 checks (c), (g)/(weaker h), (j) and return codes
rubrics_metrics.description: TestPerm2(tbl, char) returns 1 if char fails because of criterion (c) (degree divides |G|), and returns 3,4,5 if char fails because of (T3), (T4), or (T5) corresponding to (g), a weaker form of (h), and (j) respectively. It returns 0 if the character satisfies these conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TestPerm2 encodes several arithmetic and divisibility constraints; use it alongside TestPerm1 to prune impossible characters. Examples show its use on lists of candidate characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestPerm3: filtering by (h) stronger version
rubrics_metrics.description: TestPerm3(tbl, chars) returns the list of class functions in chars that satisfy criterion (h) — a stronger version of that condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use TestPerm3 to select only those candidates meeting the class-value divisibility constraints; it is more selective than the weaker checks found in TestPerm2.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestPerm4: modular tests (T8,T9) using p-block restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: TestPerm4(tbl, chars) returns those class functions in chars that satisfy (T8) and (T9) for each prime divisor p of |G|; these tests use modular representation theory and do not require decomposition matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (T8): when p divides |G| and the degree of a transitive permutation character π exactly once, the projective cover of the trivial character must be a summand of π (test omitted if projective cover cannot be identified). (T9): for permutation character π and its restriction π_B to a p-block B, for each g with g^n a p-element, π_B(g^n) is a nonnegative integer with |π_B(g)| ≤ π_B(g^n) ≤ π(g^n). TestPerm4 is useful to refine candidates using modular constraints; examples show usage on A7.

rubrics_metrics.name: TestPerm5: decomposition into projective indecomposables using Brauer table
rubrics_metrics.description: TestPerm5(tbl, chars, modtbl) requires a p-modular Brauer table modtbl and checks whether those characters in chars whose degree is divisible by the p-part of |G| can be decomposed into projective indecomposable characters; it returns the sublist that either satisfy this or to which the test does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TestPerm5 is a stronger modular test relying on explicit Brauer data; use when modtbl is available to eliminate impossible permutation characters. Example: TestPerm5(tbl, perms, tbl mod 5) returned a single surviving character for A7 examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: PermBounds: simplex boundary computation from π(g) ≥ 0 and π(1)=d
rubrics_metrics.description: PermBounds(tbl, d) computes the boundary points of the simplex of G-characters π with π(g) ≥ 0 and π(1)=d, using (inverting) a matrix similar to the rational character table. These boundary points are used by PermChars to construct all possible permutation characters of given degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computing PermBounds requires inverting large integer matrices and is feasible only for tables with a moderate number of classes (preprocessing restriction noted). PermChars either calls PermBounds or accepts precomputed bounds in its argument record.

rubrics_metrics.name: PermComb combinatorial approach and options
rubrics_metrics.description: PermComb(tbl, arec) computes possible permutation characters by an improved combinatorial approach; arec is a record that may specify degree, bounds (false to suppress bound computation), and maxmult (upper bounds on multiplicities of rational irreducibles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use arec := rec(degree := degree, bounds := false) to skip computing bounds when multiplicities are expected small. Providing maxmult can force multiplicity-free or limited-multiplicity searches. Examples show computing degree 110 solutions for M11 and restricting to multiplicity-free by setting maxmult to list of ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequalities: diagonalized system from π(g) ≥ 0 and power maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Inequalities(tbl, chars[, option]) constructs a (diagonalized) system of inequalities in the multiplicities ai of irreducible constituents from the conditions π(g) ≥ 0 and power map constraints; these guide the search for possible permutation characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The diagonalization orders rational irreducibles; the default ('straight') keeps original order (smallest degrees first), and option 'small' attempts to keep the number of intermediate inequalities small by reordering. The inequalities are used by PermChars; they can be computed once and reused via the ineq component of PermChars' cond record.

rubrics_metrics.name: PowerMap uniqueness and storage behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: PowerMap(tbl, n[, class]) returns the n-th power map of tbl if it is uniquely determined by tbl; otherwise it returns fail. Computed power maps are stored on tbl in the ComputedPowerMaps attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the character table has access to its underlying group, power maps for primes can be computed uniquely. For nearly character tables, methods can be installed to compute PowerMapOp. PowerMap checks ComputedPowerMaps before computing and stores results to avoid recomputation. Example: ComputedPowerMaps shows stored prime-power maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: PossiblePowerMaps necessary conditions for p-th power map (property 1: centralizer divisibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: For class i, the centralizer order of the image must be a multiple of the i-th centralizer order; if the elements in class i have order coprime to p then the centralizer orders of class i and its image are equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of the necessary algebraic constraints for candidate p-th power maps; it is implemented in InitPowerMap as part of PossiblePowerMaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: PossiblePowerMaps necessary conditions for p-th power map (property 2: element order behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let n be the order of elements in class i. If p divides n then the image elements have order n/p; otherwise the images have order n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion constrains possible images by element orders and is checked in InitPowerMap when building PossiblePowerMaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: PossiblePowerMaps necessary conditions for p-th power map (property 3: congruences of values)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each character χ and element g, the values χ(g^p) and GaloisCyc(χ(g), p) are algebraic integers that are congruent modulo p; if p does not divide the element order of g then the two values are equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Congruences are checked for the characters specified in options.chars (by Congruences routine). For linear characters the stronger condition χ(g)^p = χ(g^p) is checked. This uses arithmetic of character values to eliminate impossible power maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: PossiblePowerMaps necessary conditions for p-th power map (property 4: kernel behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each character χ, with kernel N, gp ∈ N for all g ∈ N; moreover if N has index p in G then gp ∈ N for all g ∈ G, and if the index of N in G is coprime to p then gp ∉ N for each g ∉ N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ConsiderKernels enforces these conditions on kernels of characters in options.chars to restrict possible images that are compatible with known normal subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: PossiblePowerMaps necessary conditions for p-th power map (property 5: use smaller power maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p is larger than the order m of an element g then the class of g^p is determined by the power maps for primes dividing the residue of p modulo m; if these smaller power maps are stored they are used to narrow possibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ConsiderSmallerPowerMaps uses precomputed ComputedPowerMaps entries for primes dividing p mod m to infer the image for large p. This reduces ambiguity when composing known prime-power maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: PossiblePowerMaps necessary conditions for p-th power map (property 6: symmetrizations yield characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each character χ of G, the symmetrization ψ defined by ψ(g) = (χ(g)^p − χ(g^p))/p must be a character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PowerMapsAllowedBySymmetrizations tests this condition and contributes to eliminating impossible power maps. The options.record.parameters control thresholds (maxamb, minamb, maxlen) that bound which characters are used in this test to manage complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: PossiblePowerMaps options record semantics (chars, powermap, decompose, quick, parameters)
rubrics_metrics.description: The optional record options for PossiblePowerMaps may include: chars (characters used for congruence/kernel/symmetrization checks; default Irr(tbl)), powermap (parametrized map approximation), decompose (whether to require symmetrizations decompose into chars), quick (stop early when single candidate remains), parameters (maxamb,minamb,maxlen controlling subroutine branching).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set decompose true when Irr(tbl) known and chars not bound; use quick=true to speed by early pruning; adjust parameters to trade completeness for speed. These options tailor the search strategy and complexity of PossiblePowerMaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: ElementOrdersPowerMap: deducing element orders from computed power maps
rubrics_metrics.description: ElementOrdersPowerMap(powermap) returns, for a list of computed p-th power maps, the order of elements in each class if uniquely determined by powermap, and Unknown(...) otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This derives OrdersClassRepresentatives when enough power maps are present; examples show filling unknowns when some power maps are missing and matching OrdersClassRepresentatives when all prime-power maps are available.
